stories.summary: On Nov 12, Compass filed 15 federal lawsuits against 15 listing databases in eight states. It accuses them of fining agents up to $15,000 for marketing homes outside the shared database. Which court hears each case will likely be decided first.
stories.title: Compass sues 15 listing databases in federal court

stories.summary: At the national Realtor group's annual meeting in New Orleans, BrokerBot won the $15,000 top prize. It builds AI helpers trained on a brokerage's own rules and files. Agents use them for deal questions, lead tracking, marketing, and admin.
stories.title: BrokerBot wins the national Realtor group's startup prize

stories.summary: The group that sets listing-data standards approved a fraud flag for its data dictionary. Listing databases can now mark a listing as fraud right in the data. The San Francisco listing database appears on none of the new certification lists.
stories.title: A fraud flag joins the data standards, and the SF database still isn't certified

stories.summary: Bangkok-based PropertyScout bought the tech and team of startup Superagent. The founder joins as chief product officer. PropertyScout wants an AI-run brokerage that automates 80% of agents' routine work. That goal is its own claim, not a proven result.
stories.title: PropertyScout buys an AI team to automate the brokerage, not license a tool

hook: The rules that decide when a listing must enter the shared database are now being fought in 15 courts at once. Which court hears each case will likely be decided first.
market_map: Today: Compass sues 15 listing databases, and BrokerBot wins the Realtor group's startup prize. A fraud flag joins the data standards, and a Bangkok brokerage buys an AI team.
one_line: The data gap before a home hits the listings.

openings.text: A growing share of homes is price-tested and shown before it ever enters the shared listing database. Compass says where that is allowed, about 48% of its sellers market first, and those homes sell for 4.6% more. Both numbers are Compass's own claims, not proven facts. A tool that records that early phase, price tests, showings, and buyer interest, would be useful no matter how the courts rule.
openings.title: The data gap before a home hits the listings

watch.text: 15 federal suits filed Nov 12. Nine listing databases already sue Compass in two New York cases. Next: a Nov 20 hearing on blocking subpoenas, and a Dec 8 deadline in a related investor suit.
watch.title: Compass v. listing databases is now the main event

watch.text: Briefs on the judge's five fairness questions are due Dec 14. The fund is $120.3M, with 132,000-plus claims, 25 opt-outs, and 2 objections. Do not cite approval.
watch.title: Tuccori: still no outcome, 12 days after the hearing

watch.text: $711,251,720.86 sits in the settlement fund as of Sept 30, 2026. About 2.7M claims have been processed. No payout date yet.
watch.title: Sitzer fund, catch-up

watch.text: John Pierpoint, 38 years at the group, says it withheld his $541,059 retirement payout after he retired in March 2025. The group denies the claim. This is an allegation, not a finding.
watch.title: Ex-finance chief sues the national Realtor group

watch.text: The proposed class narrowed to Manhattan, starting Jan 1, 2026. It alleges monopoly power from the Anywhere deal and the StreetEasy delisting. No class certified yet.
watch.title: Compass NYC rental-listings suit refiled

watch.text: No bill filed yet. Model language is in progress. Bills may come late this year or early January.
watch.title: Licensed-agent-in-the-loop campaign (from #29)

watch.text: Approved Nov 8. No listing database has adopted it yet.
watch.title: Listing-data copyright policy

watch.text: California's rental-ad disclosure law and Wisconsin's AI-photo rule take effect Jan 1, 2027. All listing-data endorsements expire the same day.
watch.title: Two deadlines land Jan 1, 2027 (48 days)

watch.text: The open questions stand. The San Francisco database is still absent from the new certification lists.
watch.title: No SF listing-database news on vendor credentialing
